title: Lock reticle: a chosen lock's brackets, and the softer in-reach reticle
oneLine: Shown/hidden and lock/reach mode of the target brackets, rebuilt on zoom change, recomputed from S each frame.
topConcern: Its update sits inside the overlays' big try: an earlier throw leaves the brackets frozen visible at their last place.

title: Stuck arrows on a monster: stuck, pinned to a texel, carried with the animation, cleared
oneLine: Each monster's predicted stuck shafts, pinned to art texels and carried frame to frame until death or respawn.
topConcern: Arrows stick on the phone's own predicted contact, never the worker's verdict: a judged miss still leaves a shaft, on that phone only.

title: Stuck-arrow bake entries: one offscreen texture per monster carrying arrows
oneLine: Per-monster baked wound texture: baked this frame, hidden, freed after 3 s unseen.
topConcern: RenderTexture keyed on exact texel size: a walking monster's moving pins can recreate it on many frames (GPU churn).

title: A player's death: the crumble, the standing skeleton, the boom, the bone pile
oneLine: Per dying player corpse: photograph, flakes fall, skeleton shivers, booms, bones settle; keyed on the death timestamp.
topConcern: A re-stamped S._deathStart (renderer seed then player_died) restarts the corpse from an already-hidden body: empty flakes, second boom.
linked: player death/respawn machine (gameEvents, wsClient, BroTown, respawn.js)

title: A monster type's sprite module: not loaded, loading, ready, let go
oneLine: Six hand-copied monster sprite modules: memoised load, swallowed failures, unload that clears tables and frees the bundle.
topConcern: A failed fetch resolves 'ready' with no art; the Wheel then draws the monster as a procedural stand-in, never retried, against its spec.

title: The lazy first-sighting kick for a variant's sheets
oneLine: Module flag plus kicked-key set that fires a variant's load once on first render; off in the Wheel.
topConcern: A kicked load is tied to no zone, so a variant a zone does not list stays loaded; retired-path only today.

title: A monster's death on its display: normal, cut, own zone death or splat; live; done
oneLine: Per-display death record keyed on the death stamp: chosen once, stepped while live, done after DUR_MS.
topConcern: Ten-input decision across five files; Done relies on the display being destroyed, so 'no display' reads as 'no death' next frame.

title: A look's own zone death: beat, pieces parting their own ways, fade, let go
oneLine: Zone-labelled death: 120 ms beat, pieces fly/pop/slump/topple/stay with bounces, fade, then freed; global live cap.
topConcern: Orphans (display destroyed mid-death) are pruned only when the next own death is considered; a few JS objects.

title: A slime's splat: flatten, spread, fade, gone
oneLine: Slime-sheet death splat: playing on its own clock, over at SPLAT_MS, disposed once.

title: Hit material bursts and the chip caches cut from the monster's own art
oneLine: Ring of particle records flying, landing by material mode, skidding, fading; LRU chip caches guarded by recent use.
topConcern: Monster chip canvases are never let go on a zone change (only prop chips are), and are plain canvases, not GPU-only.

title: Monster shots in flight and landing: atlas, per-ball record, trail, splash, marks
oneLine: Minted shot atlas lifecycle plus a record per flying ball, landing effects and capped particle/mark lists.
topConcern: The spare sprite pool is never trimmed: up to 260 hidden sprites stay in the particles layer for the page.

title: A recoloured copy of a monster's sheets: building, ready per state, freed
oneLine: Blue slime recolour cache entry: async per-sheet build, per-state readiness, free on zone exit or Wheel look release.
topConcern: Freed mid-build, the still-running closures publish ~4 MB of retinted canvases into a deleted entry nothing can free.

title: A monster hidden behind a thing, seen as its silhouette
oneLine: Per-monster silhouette riding a covering prop: shown, hidden, freed after 1.5 s or when its host goes.
topConcern: No hysteresis on the 35% cover or nearest-4 cut: edge pacing toggles visibility and parenting in a big layer.

title: Art tables that time other files' phases: snowman throw and burrow, mummy shred
oneLine: Frame splits and clamp/wrap rules for the snowman's throw and burrow and the mummy's shred; explicit halves.
topConcern: Owning slice: the burrow's tick fallback keeps a stale _burFrom and a 400 ms _burUntil, so a missed event plays wrong.
linked: snowman burrow machine (gameEvents monster_burrow, wsClient tick ph, entityRenderer)
